lessons.title: Either … or: Connecting Alternatives
lessons.content: Either … or is a correlative conjunction used to connect things of the same type — phrases, clauses, or words. It presents two alternatives where only one is true or happens.

details.explanation: Use 'either … or' to join two alternatives. The two parts joined must be of the same grammatical type.
details.example: Either he or she cooks dinner.

details.explanation: When 'either … or' connects two verbs sharing the same subject, place 'either' before the first verb.
details.example: He either washes the dishes or irons the clothes.

lessons.title: Subject-Verb Agreement with Either … or
lessons.content: If one subject is singular and the other is plural, the verb form agrees with the subject that is nearest to the verb. This is an important rule to remember when using 'either … or' with compound subjects.

details.explanation: When the two subjects joined by 'either … or' differ in number, the verb takes the form of the nearer subject.
details.example: Either my parents or my brother works hard to support the family.

details.explanation: The verb matches the number (singular or plural) of the subject closest to it.
details.example: Either the cat or the dogs are outside.
